description: California CDL delta. Air brakes, cargo, and hours stay in core_cdl.json.

questions.q: The minimum age to drive a commercial vehicle from California into another state is
questions.explanation: Interstate commerce requires the driver to be at least 21. That federal age applies to a driver leaving this state.

questions.q: You live in California and drive a CMV. Who issues the CDL?
options: The state that titled the truck
The state where the load started
questions.explanation: A CDL is issued by your state of domicile, the state where you live.

questions.q: At what weight does a 3-axle vehicle start to require a commercial driver license in California?
questions.explanation: California puts any 3-axle vehicle weighing over 6,000 pounds in commercial Class B. A basic Class C license covers a 3-axle vehicle only up to 6,000 pounds gross.

questions.q: Once you receive your initial commercial learner's permit (CLP), what is the mandatory waiting period before you are allowed to take the skills test?
questions.explanation: You must hold your commercial learner's permit for a minimum of 14 days before you are eligible to take the skills test.

questions.q: When driving on a commercial learner's permit (CLP) that includes a tank (N) endorsement, what rule applies to the tank vehicle?
options: The driver can haul non-hazardous liquids up to 1,000 gallons.
The tank must be empty, and purged if it ever held HazMat.
The driver may only operate the tank vehicle during daylight hours.
The tank must be filled with water for testing purposes.
questions.explanation: A CLP holder with an N endorsement may drive a tank vehicle only when the tank is empty. If the tank once carried hazardous materials, it must also be purged of any residue.

questions.q: Even if you are driving entirely within California (intrastate commerce), you must be at least 21 years of age if you plan to:
options: Operate a vehicle with a manual transmission.
Tow a trailer coach over 10,000 pounds.
Drive a straight truck on city streets.
questions.explanation: While drivers who are 18 can operate commercial vehicles intrastate, you must be at least 21 years old to transport hazardous materials or wastes, regardless of whether the commerce is intrastate or interstate.

questions.q: When applying for a commercial driver's license, how many chances do you have to pass the entire skills test on a single application?
questions.explanation: An applicant is allowed a total of three attempts to pass the complete skills test on one application. Failing any segment counts as one failure.

questions.q: When you give the DMV your Medical Examination Report (MER) and Medical Examiner's Certificate (MEC) with an original CLP or CDL application, how recent must they be?
questions.explanation: The DMV accepts MER and MEC forms for an original CLP or CDL only if they are dated within the past two years.

questions.q: How are traffic violation points assessed by the DMV when a driver commits an offense while operating a commercial motor vehicle?
options: Violations carry the exact same point value as noncommercial offenses.
Violations carry one and a half times the standard point count.
Violations automatically trigger a negligent operator hearing.
Violations result in double the standard point count.
questions.explanation: A traffic violation committed while driving a commercial motor vehicle carries one and a half times the normal point count compared to an infraction in a personal vehicle.

questions.q: For how long will major violations and disqualification actions remain visible on a commercial driver's California record?
questions.explanation: In California, major violations and disqualification actions are retained on a commercial driver's record for 55 years.

questions.q: Under California Air Resources Board (CARB) rules, what is the maximum time a commercial diesel vehicle over 10,001 pounds GVWR is permitted to idle for non-essential purposes?
questions.explanation: Commercial diesel vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating over 10,001 pounds are limited to just 5 minutes of non-essential idling anywhere in California.

questions.q: What is the maximum legal length for a single commercial vehicle traveling on California roads?
questions.explanation: The maximum legal length for a single motor vehicle is 40 feet, though certain exemptions exist for specific vehicle parts.

questions.q: Unless a specific exemption applies, what is the standard maximum outside width allowed for the body of a commercial vehicle or its cargo?
questions.explanation: The outside width of the vehicle's body or its load must not exceed 102 inches (8.5 feet).

questions.q: What is the maximum permitted height for a commercial vehicle and its load when measured from the road surface?
questions.explanation: The height limit for vehicles and loads in California is 14 feet, measured from the surface of the roadway.

questions.q: The handbook's general axle weight limit is 20,500 pounds for buses. What is that limit for other vehicles?
questions.explanation: The general axle limit is 20,000 pounds, with buses allowed 20,500 pounds. The tire maker's molded load limit must not be exceeded either.

questions.q: During an inspection, the California Highway Patrol will cite a driver for being overweight if the vehicle exceeds the legal weight limits (after applying a standard variation factor) by at least:
questions.explanation: CHP allows a 200-pound variation factor, but if your vehicle is 100 pounds or more overweight after that factor is applied, you will receive a citation.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit for a truck tractor with three or more axles on a California highway?
questions.explanation: In California, the maximum speed limit is 55 mph for vehicles towing another vehicle or truck tractors with three or more axles.

questions.q: When driving a larger truck, how far can you legally travel off a designated highway system onto identified exit routes to access services like food, fuel, or lodging?
questions.explanation: Larger trucks may travel up to 1 mile from identified exits or entrances on specified highways to access food, fuel, lodging, or repair services.

questions.q: If you are operating under California intrastate hours of service rules, what is the maximum amount of time you are permitted to drive after taking 10 consecutive hours off duty?
questions.explanation: Under California intrastate rules, a driver can drive up to 12 hours after completing 10 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.q: Under California intrastate rules, a driver must stop driving once they have accumulated how many on-duty hours in an 8-consecutive-day period?
questions.explanation: California's intrastate limit is 80 on-duty hours in any 8 consecutive days. Once you reach it, you may not drive.

questions.q: If you are involved in a collision resulting in an injury or property damage exceeding $1,000, within how many days must you submit a Report of Traffic Accident (SR 1) to the California DMV?
questions.explanation: You must file an SR 1 form with the DMV within 10 days if you are in an accident that causes an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.q: During your commercial driving road test, what must be done if your truck is equipped with a continuously recording video dash camera?
options: It must be turned on to record the test for DMV records.
It must be angled to only record the outside of the vehicle.
It can remain on as long as audio recording is muted.
It must be powered off, disabled, or completely blocked.
questions.explanation: Recording devices are prohibited during commercial skills tests. If a vehicle has a dash cam that cannot be powered off or disabled, it must be physically blocked.

questions.q: How will your commercial driver's license be restricted if you take your official DMV skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission?
options: You may not drive a CMV with a manual transmission.
You will be restricted to driving only within city limits.
You will not be allowed to operate air-brake equipped vehicles.
You will be required to wear corrective lenses while driving.
questions.explanation: Using an automatic transmission for the skills test automatically results in an E restriction, which prevents you from operating commercial vehicles equipped with manual transmissions.

questions.q: If you commit a second violation of the cell phone hands-free or texting law within a three-year period, for how long will you lose your commercial driving privileges?
questions.explanation: A second violation of the hands-free or texting laws within three years carries a minimum 60-day CDL disqualification.

questions.q: What is the maximum permitted overall length for a truck tractor pulling both a semitrailer and a trailer in California, assuming the trailers meet specific length restrictions?
questions.explanation: A combination consisting of a truck tractor, a semitrailer, and a trailer cannot exceed 75 feet in overall length (provided neither trailer exceeds 28.5 feet).

questions.q: Once a school bus driver reaches the age of 65, how frequently must they submit a new Medical Examination Report to the DMV?
questions.explanation: School bus drivers aged 65 and older are required to supply a new medical report to the DMV annually.

questions.q: Who is a commercial learner's permit (CLP) holder with a passenger (P) endorsement legally allowed to transport in their bus?
options: Immediate family members riding along with you.
Company employees traveling to a job site with you.
Trainees, examiners, inspectors, and the CDL holder with you.
Up to 10 regular passengers on a set route.
questions.explanation: A CLP holder with a P endorsement may not carry passengers other than federal or state auditors and inspectors, test examiners, other trainees, and the accompanying CDL holder.

questions.q: What is the minimum age required to apply for a California commercial learner's permit (CLP)?
questions.explanation: To obtain a commercial learner's permit, the applicant must be at least 18 years old.

questions.q: In California, a horse trailer with living quarters and a GVWR over 10,000 pounds requires which license?
questions.explanation: The handbook says horse trailers with living quarters and a GVWR over 10,000 pounds require a commercial Class A license. Restriction 88 is added when the truck and trailer GCWR is under 26,001 pounds.

questions.q: Apart from the recreational-trailer exceptions, California requires a CDL to tow a vehicle or trailer with a GVWR of
questions.explanation: The handbook lists towing a vehicle or trailer with a GVWR of 10,001 pounds or more among the cases that require a CDL. Non-commercial towing of a large travel trailer or trailer coach is an exception that needs a noncommercial Class A license instead.

questions.q: You tow a fifth-wheel travel trailer over 15,000 pounds GVWR, not for pay. What does California require?
options: Only a basic Class C license
questions.explanation: Towing a fifth-wheel travel trailer over 15,000 pounds GVWR, or a trailer coach over 10,000 pounds GVWR, when not for compensation is a CDL exception. The driver must have a noncommercial Class A license.

questions.q: How long is a California commercial learner's permit (CLP) valid before it must be renewed?
questions.explanation: A California CLP is valid for up to 180 days. It may be renewed for up to another 180 days, as long as the expiration date is no more than 1 year from the first application.

questions.q: A California commercial learner's permit (CLP) is valid only when you also carry
questions.explanation: The CLP is only valid when accompanied by the holder's valid California driver license, at least a noncommercial Class C. A temporary license is acceptable.

questions.q: You passed the vehicle inspection part of the CDL skills test, then renewed your CLP. What happens to that passed part?
options: It carries over to the renewed CLP
It counts only if you finish within 30 days
questions.explanation: Scores for passed skills-test segments are valid only during the first 180 days of the CLP. If the CLP is renewed, the vehicle inspection, basic control skills, and road test must be retaken.

questions.q: If you fail a CDL knowledge test in California, how long must you wait before retaking it?
options: 7 days, not counting the test day
questions.explanation: There is no waiting period to retake a failed CDL knowledge test. You get 3 attempts at the knowledge tests on one application.

questions.q: California bars school bus and transit drivers from using a cell phone for non-work purposes while driving. Which call is still allowed?
options: A call to a family member
An emergency call to the police
A call to order food for a trip
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to drive a school bus or transit vehicle while using a cell phone for non-work purposes. Emergency calls to law enforcement, a health care provider, the fire department, or other emergency services are permitted.

questions.q: In a California farm labor vehicle, who must wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: The handbook notes that the driver and all passengers in a farm labor vehicle are required to use seat belts.

questions.q: A California Youth Bus certificate covers a bus, other than a school bus, that carries no more than how many children plus the driver?
questions.explanation: A Youth Bus certificate is required to drive a bus, other than a school bus, that carries not more than 16 children and the driver to or from school, an organized non-school activity, or home.

questions.q: In what language must the California CDL skills test be taken?
options: Any language offered for the knowledge test
questions.explanation: All CDL skills tests must be conducted in English, and an interpreter is prohibited. The knowledge tests are offered in several languages.

questions.q: A road test is required to renew a California CDL that has been expired for more than
questions.explanation: The handbook lists renewing a CDL expired for more than 2 years among the cases that require a road test.

questions.q: If your passenger-transport test vehicle carries 15 persons or fewer, including the driver, your California CDL will be
options: Valid for any size of bus
questions.explanation: Your CDL is restricted to the type of vehicle used for the driving test. A passenger vehicle carrying 15 persons or fewer, including the driver, restricts you to a small size bus.

questions.q: California's Troops to Trucks program can waive the CDL skills test for qualified service members, except for
questions.explanation: Troops to Trucks lets DMV waive the CDL skills test for qualified military drivers. The skills test is not waived for an S (school bus) or P (passenger) endorsement.

questions.q: Which type of CDL does California issue?
questions.explanation: California does not issue excepted CDLs. Every driver California licenses to drive a CMV is a non-excepted driver who meets the federal qualification rules in 49 CFR 391.

questions.q: If you self-certify as Non-Excepted Intrastate (NA), what will your California CDL show?
questions.explanation: Self-certifying as Non-Excepted Intrastate puts a CDL Intrastate Only restriction (40/K) on your card and driver record. Your cargo and passengers must start and end in California.

questions.q: If you mail new medical forms (MER and MEC) to the California DMV, how far ahead of your old medical's expiration should you send them?
questions.explanation: You may take the forms to a DMV field office, or mail them to the DMV CDL Unit at least 4 weeks before your previous medical expires.

questions.q: A California commercial driver who does not pass the medical exam may still qualify for
questions.explanation: A driver who fails the medical exam may qualify for a California intrastate restricted Medical Certificate (DL 51B) by submitting the MER that shows the failed exam. California has no variances from the federal physical standards.

questions.q: In California, what is the youngest age to drive a commercial vehicle only within the state?
questions.explanation: California allows intrastate commercial driving at 18 years; interstate driving requires 21.
